label: 24-hour, 100-year storm, mid-century
description: DOT precipitation: rain in the 24-hour, 100-year storm
details: 2050–2079 · mean of GFDL-CM3 and NCAR-CCSM4 · RCP 8.5
method: Rain depth (inches) of the 24-hour storm with a 100-year return interval, 2050–2079, from SNAP's Alaska DOT precipitation-frequency projections (Rasdaman coverage dot_precip; WRF-downscaled GFDL-CM3 and NCAR-CCSM4, RCP 8.5, the only scenario). Mean of the two models; the ~480 m cells are averaged to the 1 km EPSG:3338 grid.
pros: Built for Alaska DOT design work and tied to NOAA Atlas 14 rain gauges
90 % confidence bounds exist if we want a precautionary version
cons: RCP 8.5 only, two models and 2050–2079: doesn't match the other indices
High mostly where it is always wet (South coast): more a climate map than a change signal
One storm (24 h, 100 yr) out of 15 lengths × 9 return intervals
sources: Rasdaman dot_precip pf, duration 3 (24 h), era 1, interval 100, models 0 and 1
author: Joshdpaul
retired: 2026-11-09 (Joshdpaul): depth, not change: mostly a map of where it is always wet. Letter A given to another variant (never chosen as a team decision).
